label: PF Backlog 605
title: EDP-24: Scale-out & enterprise isolation tiers (read replicas / partitioning / tenant isolation tiers / additional region cells / region-migration workflow) [EVIDENCE-GATED]

brief.problem: Enterprise scale-out requires isolation tiers, read replicas, partitioning, and multi-region cells, but there is no evidence yet quantifying the need.
brief.what_adds: Isolation tiers, read-replica routing, partitioning for hot tables, region-cell registry, and region-migration workflow.
brief.why: Supports enterprise customers with SLA and compliance requirements that exceed shared-tenant capacity.
brief.who_feels: Enterprise customers needing dedicated isolation and multi-region presence; platform team operating cells.

objective: Provide scale-out and enterprise isolation tiers including read-replica support, DB partitioning, tenant isolation tiers, additional region cells, and a safe region-migration workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Isolation tier field on tenant model drives routing to shared/dedicated DB or cell with enforced policy
Read-replica connection pool configurable per environment with automatic failover to primary on replica unavailability
Hot tables (audit/evidence) support declarative partitioning with no application query changes
Region-cell registry supports N>1 cells and region-migration dry-run + cutover + rollback using EDP-18 framework
Evidence gate satisfied with documented performance/security benchmarks before merge
in_scope: Tenant isolation tier model and enforcement
Partitioning for hot tables (audit, evidence, checkpoints)
out_of_scope: Per-tenant custom backup schedules (belongs to BI-PF-1315)
approach: Phase 1: collect evidence + decompose into sub-capabilities. Phase 2: isolation tiers + tier config alignment. Phase 3: read replicas + partitioning. Phase 4: region-cell registry + migration workflow. Each phase gated by acceptance of prior phase.
verification: Benchmark p95 query latency with/without read replica before and after
Tenant isolation penetration test across tiers
Region-migration dry-run produces zero data loss (hash/counts parity)
Partitioned table query plan regression test
Single-tenant deployments unaffected by tier code paths
risks: EVIDENCE-GATED: no concrete performance/security evidence yet quantifying need for read replicas or partitioning
Multi-region cell operations are operationally complex and hard to test locally
Partitioning strategy choice (time-based vs hash) has long-term migration implications
Region migration workflow adds operational risk if cell count > 2
rollback: Feature-flag each sub-capability (isolation tier, read replica, partitioning, region migration); disable flag to revert to single-primary single-cell behavior. Region-migration has built-in rollback snapshot via EDP-18 framework.
evidence: Existing enterprise tenant APIs and tier configs

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing enterprise tenant management APIs and DB layer: add isolation tier enum + routing to tenant models, read-replica connection pools via config, partitioning strategy for hot tables, region-cell registry building on BI-PF-1310 migration tooling, and a region-migration workflow reusing EDP-18 dual-read/cutover patterns.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1314 (readiness gate) satisfied before scale-out implementation
REQUIRES BI-PF-1315 (region-aware backup) satisfied for region cells
REQUIRES BI-PF-1312 (role separation) satisfied for read-replica DB roles
RELATED BI-PF-1310 (migration tooling) provides reusable patterns
conflict_findings: Potential concurrent DB connection-layer changes with BI-PF-1312 (role separation)
Region registry could collide with BI-PF-1315 region-aware restore if both add region metadata independently — coordinate
Tenant model modifications must not race with BI-PF-1300 role changes
duplication_findings: Region migration workflow partially overlaps BI-PF-1310 (EDP-18) — reuse its dry-run/rollback/cutover framework
Isolation tiers must align with hardware-tiers.json and licensing-tiers.json already in config layer
Region-aware restore already in BI-PF-1315 — complement, do not rebuild
analysis.rationale: This is a broad scale-out initiative spanning five sub-capabilities. It reuses existing enterprise tenant infrastructure, tier configs, and migration tooling. However it is EVIDENCE-GATED with no concrete performance data yet, so it should remain blocked pending evidence collection and sub-capability decomposition before implementation begins.
assumptions: PostgreSQL is the target DB and supports read replicas / partitioning natively
Existing tenant model can carry an isolation_tier column without breaking single-tenant deployments
BI-PF-1310 migration framework will be available as a reusable substrate
Enterprise customers will drive region cell requirements with concrete SLAs
risks: EVIDENCE-GATED: no concrete performance/security evidence yet quantifying need for read replicas or partitioning
Multi-region cell operations are operationally complex and hard to test locally
Partitioning strategy choice (time-based vs hash) has long-term migration implications
Region migration workflow adds operational risk if cell count > 2
evidence: Existing enterprise tenant APIs and tier configs
missing_info: Concrete evidence thresholds triggering read replicas vs partitioning (query latency, storage size)
Which isolation tiers are required (shared-pool / dedicated-DB / dedicated-cell)?
Target cloud providers and region-cell topology for initial rollout
Whether partitioning targets are time-series tables (evidence, audit) or entity tables

missing: Target cloud/region topology and isolation tier definitions
context_review.reason: Item is explicitly EVIDENCE-GATED. Without quantified evidence for read replicas, partitioning, or additional cells, and without sub-capability decomposition, implementation cannot proceed in a deterministic manner.
